newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds stable as market awaits FOMC decision.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds stable as market awaits FOMC decision.

text.p: Irish government bonds held onto their previous closing levels in patchy trade on Tuesday as the market prepared for the FOMC's (Federal Open Market Committee) decision on U.S. interest rates, dealers said.

"Wednesday morning trade will carry the fallout from the FOMC. Dublin is trading less than 100 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area and this would normally be signal for some selling but it hasn't happened yet," one dealer said.
By 1515 GMT the eight percent bond due 2001 was up seven pence at 104.88 to yield 6.49 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 was unchanged at 103.65 to yield 7.06 percent.
"For the first time in several days the Irish market hasn't performed as well as in Germany or in the UK," the dealer added.

In the UK, gilts were unchanged despite a rumour-ridden prelude to the FOMC decision in the U.S. London dealers said the market was unaffected by rumours that the UK Chancellor was resigning. British Treasury officials said the rumours were "nonsense".
In the U.S., August import prices fell by 0.2 percent on July while export prices fell 0.1 percent.
